result: LPS-stimulated PBMCs from CFS patients released more IL-1beta, IL-6 and TNF-alpha (P<0.05), and more IL-6 to PHA (P<0.01), while LPS-stimulated TGF-beta release was lower; serum TGF-beta was higher (290 vs 104 pg/mL, P<0.01).
reason: Independent cohort showing exaggerated stimulated innate cytokine release to a microbial antigen (LPS), the core of the finding; PBMC rather than whole blood and no exercise arm; the serum TGF-beta result relates to immune-tgfbeta-artefact.

result: In 13 CFS patients vs 13 healthy and 7 IBS controls, blood lactate was significantly higher at the same submaximal treadmill stage (stage III), with higher submaximal heart rate and Borg score (8.2 vs 6.6 and 5.3).
reason: Higher lactate at a fixed workload stage is the lactate-per-workload measure the finding names; very small sample.

result: On a symptom-limited treadmill test with gas analysis, 13 CFS patients had reduced aerobic work capacity and shorter time on the treadmill than normal and IBS controls.
reason: Same maximal-test measure of reduced aerobic capacity in an independent cohort, though the abstract gives no peak VO2 or peak heart rate values and the sample is tiny.

result: In 41 patients vs matched controls, resting ECG, 24 h rhythm, LV dimensions and fractional shortening were normal, but on graded exercise only 4/31 patients vs 20/32 controls reached target heart rate, peak HR was 124 vs 152 bpm (66% vs 82% of age-maximum, p<0.0001) and exercise lasted 9 vs 12 min.
reason: The main result is chronotropic incompetence on a maximal test (low-peak-vo2 finding); its normal resting echo LV dimensions only weakly contradict the small-heart finding, which rests on volumes and stroke volume that were not measured.

result: In 41 CFS patients vs 23 controls, most patients had low NKH1+T3- NK cell numbers and consistently low cytotoxicity against several targets; IL-2 raised killing of K562 but most patients still could not lyse EBV-infected B cells.
reason: Independent early cohort with the same NK cytotoxicity measure showing a reduction, matching the meta-analysed arm of the contested finding; not among the cited studies.
